The Stoic Week

Every autumn thousands of people spend a week living like a Stoic. They read a short passage each morning, write down what is in their control, and review the day each evening. The exercise is simple, and that is the point: it is meant to fit into an ordinary life.

What people report

Participants describe small changes rather than revelations. They notice they argue less with traffic, they sleep a little better, and they find it easier to let go of the opinions of strangers. Most say the evening review is the part they keep doing after the week ends.

The dichotomy of control does most of the work. Sorting worries into what you can change and what you cannot turns a vague unease into a short list, and a short list is something you can act on.
